lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions about your circumstances.

First of all, could you please tell me how many children you're looking to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names and ages?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! I'm looking to claim for my son Alex. He's 18 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information about Alex.

Since Alex is 18 years old, eligibility for Child Benefit depends on whether he is currently in approved education or training.

Could you please tell me if Alex is currently in any of the following:
- Full-time non-advanced education (such as A-levels, T-levels, or Scottish Highers)
- Approved training (not funded by an employer)

Or has he left education/training, started working, or started an apprenticeship?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex isn't in any education or training at the moment. He finished school and isn't doing A-levels or anything like that.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that.

Since Alex has left education and isn't in approved training, I have a couple more questions:

1. Has Alex registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services since leaving education? (If so, and if he's done this recently, Child Benefit could potentially continue for up to 20 weeks.)

2. Has Alex started paid work for 24 hours or more a week, or started receiving any benefits in his own right (such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he hasn't registered with any careers service or the armed forces. And he's not working - certainly not 24 hours a week or anything like that. He's not getting any benefits in his own name either.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information.

Unfortunately, based on what you've told me, it appears that Alex would not be eligible for Child Benefit. Here's why:

For children aged 16 or over, Child Benefit normally only continues if the child:
- Stays in **approved education or training**, OR
- Has registered with a **government-sponsored careers service** or the **armed services** within 20 weeks of leaving education (for 16 or 17 year olds only - and Alex is 18)

Since Alex is 18, has finished school, is not in approved education or training, and hasn't registered with a careers service or the armed forces, he unfortunately no longer meets the eligibility criteria for Child Benefit.

Before I confirm my assessment, could I just check: do you live in the UK?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that.

Based on all the information you've provided, I'm now ready to give you my assessment on your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on all the information you've provided, I'm afraid you are **not eligible** for Child Benefit for Alex.

**Reason:**

Alex is 18 years old and is no longer in approved education or training. For children aged 16 or over, Child Benefit can only continue if the child remains in approved education or training (such as A-levels or equivalent) until they turn 20.

The option to extend Child Benefit for 20 weeks by registering with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services is only available to 16 or 17 year olds, so this doesn't apply to Alex at age 18.

**What you could do:**

If Alex's circumstances change in the future—for example, if he decides to enrol in approved education or training—you may wish to check your eligibility again at that time.

I'm sorry I couldn't bring you better news. Is there anything else I can help you with?
